1.5.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the policy defines forms of violence (Pasal 4) as including “penelantaran” (neglect) and “eksploitasi” (exploitation), but it does not explicitly define or name “kekerasan ekonomi” (economic violence) as a distinct form. The only explicit economic-related harm is in the definition of “Korban tindak kekerasan” (Pasal 1 angka 15) which includes “kerugian ekonomi” (economic loss) as a possible impact on victims, and several provisions about “pemberdayaan ekonomi” (economic empowerment) as part of recovery/prevention (e.g., Pasal 18 huruf g; Pasal 22). Those are not the same as explicitly recognizing economic violence as a violence type. Given the retrieved English passages (which accurately reflect these points), a ‘No’ is reasonable; the golden ‘Yes’ likely over-interprets economic empowerment/economic loss as ‘economic violence’.

1.9.evaluator_rationale: Although the policy mentions sexual violence and exploitation generally, none of the candidate sentences explicitly refer to sexual exploitation or sexual slavery as such.
